title: Over 1,200 Arrested in France as Nationwide Protests Turn Violent
snippet: Protests over school conditions and rising costs devolved into chaos across France on Saturday, leaving historical buildings ablaze, shops looted, and over a thousand in custody.
content:
PARIS — Demonstrations over soaring living costs and deteriorating public school conditions erupted into violent unrest across France on Saturday, leaving historic landmarks torched, local businesses looted, and more than 1,200 people in custody.

French authorities reported that roughly 550,000 people took to the streets nationwide. While daytime rallies began largely peacefully, tensions boiled over by nightfall. In Paris, riot police responded with tear gas and water cannons as groups of agitators set vehicles on fire and erected barricades near the iconic Place de la République.

Historic Landmarks Torched, Stores Ransacked

The violence inflicted severe damage across several major French cities. In Limoges, a massive blaze engulfed the town hall, causing a partial collapse of the building's roof. Officials in Lyon expressed heartbreak after hostile crowds set the city's historic tourist center on fire and obstructed firefighters from safely tackling the flames.

Looters also targeted commercial hubs. In Lille, an Apple store was broken into and emptied, while numerous clothing and grocery stores were ransacked across Paris.

Human Toll and Political Escalation

According to French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu, at least 150 law enforcement officers sustained injuries during the clashes. Serious casualties were also reported among protesters; in Saint-Étienne, a young man lost his hand to an explosive grenade during the commotion, local officials confirmed.

The protests initially stemmed from weeks of student demonstrations against staff shortages and dilapidated infrastructure in the country's high schools. However, the crowds were significantly bolstered Saturday by trade unionists and members of the "yellow vest" movement, a populist group known for cost-of-living demonstrations.

The outbreak of violence comes during a period of intense political uncertainty as France prepares for next year's presidential election. President Emmanuel Macron vowed that rioters will be brought to justice, declaring that those who attacked municipal buildings and businesses "will be prosecuted and punished."
